# Model card: Rubric scoring

| | |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Score each rubric criterion of an application against the locked rubric, with evidence, so a person can review faster. |
| Workflow | hire |
| Code | `pairly_hire.scoring.model`, aggregation in `pairly_hire.scoring.aggregate` |
| Prompt | `hire_cv_score` version `v1`, file SHA-256 `de4806a306cf2b26...` |
| Output schema | `CvScoreOutput` |
| Model tiers, cheapest first | `small` (anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, openai `gpt-6-luna`) then `large` (anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5`, openai `gpt-6.1-sol`) |
| Temperature | 0.0 |
| Output token limit | 4096 |
| Confidence threshold to accept | 0.5 |

## Inputs

The locked rubric (criteria, evidence descriptions, score anchors; no weights) and the blinded CV text: names, contact details and protected markers replaced. Never the self-identification answers.

## Outputs

Per criterion: a score on the rubric scale, a confidence, verbatim evidence quotes and a short reason it is not higher. The overall score is computed in code from the criterion scores, never by the model.

## Human oversight

The score is a suggestion on the shortlist screen. A person shortlists or not (`decide`, second factor); nothing is rejected automatically. A person can override a score, which is recorded as its own decision and feeds calibration.

## Limits

* Agreement with people is measured on synthetic labels, not on real hiring outcomes.
* Low confidence escalates to the larger tier; if no tier is confident, the criterion is not scored and a person decides.
* A CV with guardrail findings is scored on sanitised text and flagged for review.
* Every call is logged in `model_calls` (prompt version and hash, model, inputs, output, tokens, cost) and fails closed: no model means a person does the step.

Numbers come only from result files committed in `evals/results/`, exactly as written there. See [evals.md](../evals.md) for what each run measures. In the scripted files (`hire.json`, `pay.json`) a model metric stays pending; live numbers are read from the committed `*_live.json` files, and the ones with a founder-approved threshold (`live: true` in `evals/thresholds.yaml`) gate.

* Evidence validity (recorded run): Scripted answers: proves the evidence checks, not the model.
* Largest overall score change across a pair, scripted answers: Tests the deterministic part (redaction, evidence, aggregation), not a model.
* Largest change on pairs with byte-identical scoring input (live run): With identical input, a change is the model's own run-to-run variation, not the swapped attribute.
